critiques.summary: H1 (dep-5101 order-service v2.14.0 margin-check rewrite → NPE 'marginProfile is null' on FNO orders → HTTP 500) is the best-supported and adequately proven origin. The chain is short and rests on verified observations at every hop: dep-5101 is the sole deploy/config change across all services in the window (F1, F4, F30, F33, F34), its changelog is a margin-check rewrite in the exact POST /v1/orders validation path scoped to F&O orders (F2, F30), the NPE occurs in the class it introduced at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 orderType=FNO (F10, F28, F30), onset tracks the deploy (12:10Z deploy → 12:12Z metric step → first error 12:12:31Z, F3, F8, F10), and the failure persists on a flat ~18% plateau for ~104 minutes with no traffic/resource correlate (F9, F12). Alternatives are contradicted by data rather than merely dismissed: all six non-order services stay flat at ~0.1-0.32% with no step at 12:12Z (F20), redis-cache and ledger-db legs are flat (F24-F26, F29), request/latency/cpu/pool are flat excluding saturation and load (F12), and ledger-db co-tenancy would have shown a multi-writer signature that is absent (F32). H2 retains one wholly unevidenced hop requiring a change invisible to the change registry. My two prior blockers are closed as far as this incident's telemetry permits: blast radius is now measured, and the decisive pre-onset-success discriminator was conclusively shown to be non-executable (order-service emits no non-ERROR margin/FNO lines, F42/F43/F46), so it is an assumption/lower-cap matter, not a reason to continue. Residual limits: no source diff (permanent tooling gap) so the mechanism is inferred from log text; the sub-reading (missing null guard vs unpopulated field) is unresolved and may imply a backfill in addition to rollback; and the absence of a restart provides no corroboration that the deploy was activated in-process.
